input.title: The Eclipse Prince
input.script_text: EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY A circular sand arena ringed by carved stone stands, sun-emblem banners everywhere. The royal throne canopy stands on a raised marble dais at the north end, overlooking the arena; directly beside it is a separate covered stand where the royal courtiers sit. Citizens crowd the stone stands on the other sides, and the grand entrance gate is at the south end, facing the throne. Citizens wear simple cotton dhotis and sarees; courtiers wear silk angavastrams and turbans. Characters: Prince Ranvijay, Ranvijay's Horse, Rajguru Badrinath, Maharaja Someshwar, Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens A ROYAL GONG crashes. Citizens press against the arena railing and raise sun-emblem flags. PRINCE RANVIJAY (early 20s, fair-to-wheatish skin, broad shoulders, wearing golden royal armour and a small crownlet) rides into the arena on RANVIJAY'S HORSE (a jet-black Marwari stallion, red-and-gold saddle cloth). He trots across the sand toward the north end. Brass bells on the reins ring. Ranvijay raises his jeweled sword toward the crowd. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Dekho dekho kaun aaya...Suryagarh ka sher aaya...Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay, Rajkumar Ranvijay ki jay Prince Ranvijay halts his horse in front of the royal courtier seating area and looks towards the stand. PRINCE RANVIJAY (booming, playful) Dekha, rajguru? mere aagman bhar se hi praja mein sahas aur utsaah ki lahar daud gayi.. Standing at the front rail of the courtiers' stand, closest to the throne dais, is RAJGURU BADRINATH (60s, bald, flame-and-lotus scalp tattoo, white beard, saffron robes, rudraksha beads) who raises both hands toward Ranvijay. RAJGURU BADRINATH (smooth, ceremonial) ye toh hona hi tha rajkumar, sampoorna rajya is baat ko bhalibhati jaanta hai ki Swarnadweep ke asli rakshak aap hi hai. PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, smug) rakshak nahi rajguru ..main is rajya ka hone wala samraat hun aur ye praja meri daas... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (60s, dusky skin, weathered face, gold robes and silver beard) sits on his throne on the raised dais beneath the sun-carved canopy, just beside the courtiers' stand, looking down at Ranvijay. He strikes the armrest with his ring. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) swagat kijiye aapke hone wale samraat ka.. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR points his hands towards Ranvijay, Their eyes meet and both smile. The citizens start cheering his name again. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jay! Ranvijay raises his hands and takes their appreciation. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, formal) Poore rajya mein koi hai jo Yuvraj Ranvijay ko chunauti de sake? EXT. RAJMAHAL - DAY (CONTINUOUS) We see the sprawling view of a grand royal palace with endless rooms. INT. RAJMAHAL - AGNIVESH'S READING ROOM - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh A quiet room filled with bookshelves lined with ancient books. AGNIVESH (24, royal-blue angrakha, ivory dhoti, maroon angavastram, worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist) sits in shadow by a narrow window, slowly turning the pages of an ancient book. Hearing the distant roar from the arena, Agnivesh closes the book, rises and walks out through the hallway, book in hand. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens Citizens are cheering and making noise. In the courtiers' stand beside the throne dais, the Royal Courtiers sit chanting. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (chanting, mocking) Agnivesh! Agnivesh! Agnivesh CUT TO EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION ENTRANCE - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh We see a back view of Agnivesh walking toward the Grand Royal Arena with an ancient book in his hand as the massive royal door opens. Transitioning to a front entry view, Agnivesh steps through the grand entrance into the arena, holding the ancient book in hand and a worn ANCESTRAL SWORD hanging at his waist. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Ranvijay's Horse, Maharaja Someshwar, Rajguru Badrinath, Devika, Royal Guard, Citizen, Several Citizens, Several Royal Courtiers Maharaja Someshwar sits on his throne on the dais, a ROYAL GUARD at attention beside him holding the tall royal sun banner. Rajguru Badrinath stands at the front rail of the courtiers' stand. Ranvijay is still on horseback in front of the stand. From his saddle, Ranvijay turns towards the south gate. AGNIVESH walks across the sand toward him, reading the book in his hand, the worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist. PRINCE RANVIJAY (calling down, taunting, laughing) jise tum sab yuddh ke liye bula rahe ho vo koi yoddha nahi balki ek durbal aur kaayar naari ke samaan hai.... Rajguru Badrinath turns from the courtiers' stand toward the Maharaja on the dais. RAJGURU BADRINATH (soft, poisonous) kaayaron ko yuddh se door hi rakhna chahiye maharaj. Main aapse anurodh karta hun Yuvraj Ranvijay ko is rajya ka hone wala samraat ghoshit kiya jaaye. The citizens laugh at him and whisper to each other. A CITIZEN leaning over the railing of the stone stands calls out. CITIZEN (mocking) haar ke dar se.. haath mein kitaab leke aaya hai... Agnivesh stops on the sand in front of Ranvijay's horse, just below the throne dais, closes his book, bends down and places it on the sandy ground. He rises, looks up towards Maharaja Someshwar on the dais and greets him with folded hands. For a split second, his right sleeve shifts up, revealing a faint golden SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist. He tugs the sleeve back down. AGNIVESH (steady, respectful) Pranaam Pitashri. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (hard, loud) HUH... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (feeling agony) Tujh jaise kaayar aur darpook insaan ko apna putra kahna .. aa thuuu.. ye mera aur poori praja ka apmaan hai.. Agnivesh straightens. The citizens are quiet now. AGNIVESH (low, controlled) Pitashri..Yeh mera bhi rajya hai aur main is rajya ka vaasi hu..mujhe bhi apna samarthya dikhaane ka mauka milna chahiye Agnivesh turns to his brother Ranvijay, places his right fist and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its sheath. His wrist mark flares beneath his sleeve, a jolt runs up his arm, and the sword slips from his hand and falls. everyone starts laughing loudly, Maharaja Someshwar also feeling the same. PRINCE RANVIJAY (laughing, sharp) ye tera rajya hai na?....to Ja aur rajya ke logo ka mal mootra saaf kar ke rajya ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar. kyunki tujh jaise insaan se yuddh karna to mere liye hi apmaan ki baat hai.. RAJGURU BADRINATH (arrogent, public) Rajkumar ek dam sahi kah rahe hain. Mrityu Grahan mein janma balak na to rajya ka varis ho skata hai aur na hi is pratiyogita me bhaag le sakta hai.., yahi niyam hai. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (murmuring, uneasy) Mrityu Grahan ... awwww.. kya ye sach hai? AGNIVESH (firm, restrained) janm se koi bhi apraadhi nahi hota raajguru, aur na hi janm lena koi apraadh hai. Agnivesh looks towards Maharaja Someshwar Maharaja Someshwar rises from his throne in anger, towering over Agnivesh from the dais. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, cutting) Tu janm lete hi apni maa ko nigal gya .. yahi tera sabse bada apraadh hai. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (louder, cruelly formal) Tujhe is Rajmahal aur is rajya mein bas teri mari hui maa aur meri kripa ki wajah se rahne diya gaya hai. Agnivesh falls down on his knees just right besides the Ancestor Sword, he joins his hands and starts pleading to his father Maharaja Someshwar. AGNIVESH (voice tight, respectful) Aapko poori praja ke saamne yun mera uphaas nahi karna chahiye maharaj. Maharaja Someshwar raises his hand. The ROYAL GUARD beside the throne lowers the royal sun banner. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, public) main Iss rajya ka Maharaj, tujhe ye aadesh deta hun...ki tu apni maa ki ye mahaan talwaar abhi Ranvijay ko saunp de. ye talwaar ek sacche rajkumaar ke haath mein hi shobha deti hai naaki tujh jaise kaayar aur shraapit insaan ke... Agnivesh picks up his sword, gets up and grips the hilt. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Ranvijay steps down from his horse, walks towards Agnivesh and holds out his palm without looking at Agnivesh. PRINCE RANVIJAY (quiet, arrogant) Ye talwaar mujhe de de Agnivesh.. AGNIVESH (voice deep, controlled) Ye talwaar tumhe sweekar hi nahi karegi..kyuki tum iske laayak hi nahi ho. In fear that a fight might break out between the two, the people standing around start breaking out in a nervous sweat. Everybody looking at Ranvijay’s open palm. Maharaja Someshwar steps forward to the edge of the dais and points his finger at Agnivesh. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (anger , shouting) Agnivesh........... Talwar Ranvijay ko saunp do anyatha tumhe abhi mrityu dand diya jaayega.. A pause. Someshwar surveys the whole arena. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, final) Ab koi pratiyogita nahi hogi.kyuki tum pratiyogita ke kaabil hi nahi ho. yahi hamara antim nirnay hai. Agnivesh slowly raises the ANCESTRAL SWORD, holds it upright before his chest, then lays it across Ranvijay’s waiting palms. Ranvijay closes his fingers around the sword. He raises it for the court. PRINCE RANVIJAY (triumphant, loud) aakhirkar is talwaar ko apna asli maalik mil hi gaya.. The citizens and royal courtiers laugh at Agnivesh. Among the laughing courtiers in the stand behind the Rajguru, one does not smile: DEVIKA (22, turquoise-and-gold warrior attire, a short curved dagger at her belt), the Rajguru's niece. Her eyes stay on Agnivesh. Agnivesh lowers his empty hand. CLOSE ON his right wrist: his sleeve slides back, revealing the SWORD-SHAPED MARK burning molten gold, its heat scorching the silk cuff. HARD CUT

Director Production Plan: Episode 1 — The Eclipse Prince
① Theme, Premise & Narrative Core
Core Theme: Sovereign legitimacy is born from enduring sacrificial humiliation, not inherited thrones or martial arrogance.
Emotional Arc (Three Tiers):
Tier 1 (Martial Vaunt vs. Ascetic Quiet): Ranvijay projects broad, chest-forward pomp on horseback while Agnivesh maintains stillness, measured finger movements, and steady breathing over ancient manuscripts.
Tier 2 (The Crucible of Public Shaming): Physical escalation from standing defiance to kneeling in the arena sand with open, surrendered palms under imperial decree.
Tier 3 (Primordial Awakening): Complete stillness masking subterranean fury; the jaw locks, breathing suspends, and the dormant wrist seal ignites beneath scorched silk.
Audience Takeaway & Emotional Strategy: Cultivate acute cathartic anticipation. By driving filial rejection and brotherly arrogance to an unbearable peak, the audience is primed to crave ruthless karmic retribution, sealed by a supernatural physical cliffhanger.
② Visual Style & Framing Tone (16:9 Landscape with 9:16 Safe Area)
Compositional Grammar (16:9 Framing with Central 9:16 Safe Area):
Center-Weighted Safe Area Staging: The primary dramatic subjects, key physical blocking, eyelines, and critical micro-expressions are tightly locked within the central 9:16 vertical safe zone, ensuring full compositional integrity when cropped vertically for mobile microdrama platforms.
Horizontal Wings for Environmental Scale: The flanking left and right thirds of the 16:9 horizontal frame are dedicated to spatial scale—soaring sandstone colonnades, tiered spectator stands, billowing sun-mandala standards, and distant palace towers.
Vertical Stacking within Center Zone: Exploit the vertical depth of the central safe area to enforce hierarchy: Maharaja Someshwar commands the upper third on the elevated dais; Ranvijay commands the center third on horseback; Agnivesh occupies the lower third kneeling on the sand.
Frame-within-Frame: Use massive carved sandstone archways, gate thresholds, and marble pavilion pillars to enclose figures within the central safe area.
Three-Layer Spatial Depth:
Foreground: Ringing brass bridle bells, sand drifts, stone balustrades, or the ornate jade sword hilt placed close to the lens.
Midground: Primary actors executing smooth physical blocking—kneeling, mounting, drawing weapons, passing objects between open hands.
Background: Stacked spectator galleries, palace facades, and mountain waterfalls establishing monumental architecture.
Camera Movement & Dynamic Rhythm:
Camera Grammar: Exclusively smooth, controlled mechanical movements. Gliding dolly tracks, slow vertical crane pedestals, smooth jib arcs, and stable locked-off tripod shots.
Strict Exclusions: Zero handheld shake, zero whip-pans, zero crash zooms, and zero erratic camera jitter. Every motion begins and decelerates with silky, cinematic precision.
Dolly Push / Pull: Smooth, slow linear dolly push-ins to intensify psychological weight on crucial dialogue turns; smooth dolly pull-backs to reveal isolation against oppressive court grandeur.
Crane Pedestal: Vertical crane elevations tracking the power gradient between the high northern royal dais and the arena floor below.
③ Narrative Structure & Rhythm Planning (38 Shots / 286 Seconds)
Narrative Model Selection: High-Impact Historical Indian Fantasy Microdrama (Hook-and-Reversal Structure).
Global Rhythm & Scale: 38 planned shots across 6 continuous narrative beats, totaling exactly 286 seconds (average shot duration ~7.5 seconds, allowing rich physical acting beats, uninterrupted dialogue delivery, and deliberate camera glides).
Beat Division & Episode Pacing Table:



Beat #	Beat Name	Scene / Setting	Core Narrative Event	Shots	Duration	Emotional Density	Camera Rhythm
01	The Sun Prince's Vaunt	Royal Tournament Pavilion	Ranvijay parades on stallion; Someshwar endorses martial supremacy.	6	45s	High (Arrogant Triumph)	Gliding dolly tracks & sweeping crane descent
02	The Quiet Anomaly	Agnivesh's Reading Room & Gate	Agnivesh closes tome upon hearing roars; walks through corridor to gate.	6	42s	Medium (Measured Contrast)	Slow linear push-in & steady lateral dolly track
03	Trial of the Scholar	Royal Tournament Pavilion	Arena mocks the book; Agnivesh lays it on sand and salutes his unyielding father.	6	45s	High (Hostile Derision)	Controlled counter-tracks & locked-off medium cuts
04	The Severed Bond	Royal Tournament Pavilion	Agnivesh attempts to draw blade; weapon clatters to sand; Someshwar disowns him.	7	52s	Extreme (Seismic Humiliation)	Smooth downward jib tilts & tense static holds
05	The Extorted Blade	Royal Tournament Pavilion	Agnivesh kneels under execution threat; transfers heirloom blade to Ranvijay.	7	54s	Extreme (Suppressed Defiance)	Slow horizontal dolly & precise creeping close-ups
06	The Molten Seal	Royal Tournament Pavilion	Ranvijay hoists blade; Devika observes with dread; Agnivesh's wrist seal ignites.	6	48s	Climax (Awakening Cliffhanger)	Gliding arc track & slow macro push-in
Total	Full Episode Arc	Continuous Production	Complete Exposition to Primordial Awakening	38	286s	Cumulative Escalation	Smooth Mechanical Precision
Key Visual Turning Points:
The Dropped Blade: Agnivesh attempts to draw; a sudden involuntary wrist spasm sends the heirloom clattering onto the sand, visually validating the crowd's mockery before the true seal awakens.
The Descent to Knees: Agnivesh drops down before the royal dais, visually concretizing royal subjugation.
The Horizontal Transfer: The blade rests across outstretched palms from brother to brother.
The Searing Cuff: Slow, creeping macro glide to Agnivesh's silk sleeve scorching and blackening as the divine golden brand flares beneath.
④ Scene-by-Scene Emotion & Visual Intent
Scene 1: Royal Tournament Pavilion — The Arrogant Parade (Shots 1–6 / 45s)
Emotional Objective: Unchecked martial hubris; squared shoulders, lifted chin, smirking eye-locks.
Atmospheric Direction: Oppressive courtly pomp, intoxicating hubris, celebratory adulation.
Camera Intent: Smooth crane arm lowering from the high arena rim to an eye-level tracking dolly before the warhorse, capturing Ranvijay centered within the 9:16 safe area while the 16:9 wings capture cheering tiers.
Spatial Narrative: Ranvijay commands the central sand runway; Someshwar towers on the high northern throne dais.
Distance Design: Wide arena vista gliding smoothly into medium tracking of the stallion and close-up smirks.
Scene 2: Agnivesh's Reading Room — The Still Center (Shots 7–10 / 28s)
Emotional Objective: Deep meditative composure; slow turning of aged parchment; eyes tranquil despite distant roars.
Atmospheric Direction: Secluded gravitas, scholastic isolation.
Camera Intent: Slow linear dolly push-in toward Agnivesh seated in the window alcove, followed by a steady lateral slider tracking his deliberate stride toward the arched door.
Spatial Narrative: Claustrophobic stone interior framed by vertical shelves, insulating Agnivesh from the martial frenzy outside.
Distance Design: Macro detail of fingers on binding → Medium waist-level glide → Smooth follow shot to the threshold.
Scene 3: Royal Tournament Pavilion Entrance — The Scholar's Walk (Shots 11–12 / 14s)
Emotional Objective: Unshakable resolve stepping directly into hostility; steady, unhurried stride.
Atmospheric Direction: Imposing threshold, hostile public exposure.
Camera Intent: Symmetrical wide track positioned along the central corridor, following Agnivesh's back as the colossal gates smoothly part, gliding forward onto the bright sand threshold.
Spatial Narrative: Southern portal aligns directly on the cardinal axis facing the northern throne dais.
Distance Design: Wide threshold frame transitioning via forward dolly to a medium full-body profile.
Scene 4: Royal Tournament Pavilion — The Public Shaming & Blade Surrender (Shots 13–38 / 199s)
Emotional Objective: Venomous filial disgust from the king; cold gloating from Ranvijay; compressed righteous fury behind Agnivesh's locked jaw.
Atmospheric Direction: Visceral court tribunal, severe humiliation, supernatural dread.
Camera Intent:
Slow crane pedestal moving vertically between Someshwar's commanding downward gaze and Agnivesh's upright posture.
Smooth lateral slider passes tracking Ranvijay circling on the sand.
Stable locked-off medium close-ups on Rajguru's calculating smirk and Devika's unsmiling eyes.
Deliberate mechanical creep-in to the horizontal blade resting on open palms.
Slow, steady macro dolly toward Agnivesh's singeing cuff as the molten-gold brand activates.
Spatial Narrative: Triangular standoff: Someshwar elevated on the dais, Ranvijay standing over the sand, Agnivesh pinned on his knees between them.
Distance Design: Medium confrontation masters tightening systematically into intimate close-ups of eyes, clenched jaws, open hands, and radiant skin.
⑤ Diegetic Sound Direction (No Music / Pure SFX)
Concrete Environmental Soundscapes:
Arena Textures: Clinking brass bridle bells on horse tack; iron horseshoes crunching coarse sand; linen sun banners snapping in gusts.
Courtly & Crowd Textures: Wooden staff striking stone flags; collective guttural jeers bouncing off high stone tiers; gold bangles rattling on stone railings.
Weapon Handling: Crisp rasp of blade sliding against scabbard throat; heavy metallic thud of the sword clattering onto packed sand; dry crackle of scorching silk fibers.
Key Silence Moments:
Complete drop of arena crowd ambient noise when Agnivesh utters "Pitashri."
Absolute one-second audio vacuum the moment the sword hits the sand.
Elimination of crowd cheers at the climax, isolating only the dry, sizzling burn of heated silk against flesh.
⑥ Transitions & Visual Continuity Anchors
Transition Strategy:
Scene 1 to Scene 2: Sound bridge: Ranvijay's booming laugh dissolves into the dry rustle of turning parchment inside the reading room.
Scene 2 to Scene 3: Match cut: Hand closing the leather manuscript cuts directly to the book gripped at Agnivesh's hip at the gateway.
Scene 3 to Scene 4: Spatial continuity: Sand threshold extends directly into the wide tournament arena circle.
Scene 4 Climax: Hard blackout cut mid-sizzle on the glowing wrist mark, leaving the turn unresolved.
Visual Continuity Anchors:
Ancestral Sword: White jade hilt carved with makara heads, gold lotus-bud pommel, and pale silver wootz steel ripple preserved across drawing, dropping, and handover.
Ancient Book: Deep maroon leather binding with embossed faded gold sun mandala held in Agnivesh's left hand and placed on the sand.
Wardrobe State: Agnivesh's royal-blue silk angrakha sleeves remain fastened at the wrists until the cuff scorches and draws back at the cliffhanger.
⑦ Derivative Asset Pre-Planning List



Asset Name	Derivative State	Reason / Appearing Segment
Royal Tournament Pavilion	Reverse Arena View	Facing South Grand Entrance Gate from the northern throne dais; required for Agnivesh's walk-in and crowd jeering coverage (Sc 1, Sc 3, Sc 4)
Royal Tournament Pavilion	Low-Angle Dais View	Steep upward perspective looking from sand arena up to Maharaja Someshwar's elevated throne canopy; essential for vertical confrontation beats (Sc 4)
Agnivesh's Reading Room	Window Alcove Reverse View	Looking from the narrow carved window back into the shadowy room's bookshelves; required for Agnivesh's rising and exit blocking (Sc 2)
Royal Tournament Pavilion Entrance	Interior Gate Facing Arena View	Perspective positioned within the threshold corridor looking outward into the bright sand arena (Sc 3)
Agnivesh	Glowing Wrist Mark State	Right sleeve cuff singed and rolled back, exposing the burning molten-gold sword-shaped brand on skin; essential for episode climax cliffhanger (Sc 4)
Ancestral Sword	Drawn Blade State	Blade unsheathed from scabbard, displaying the bare silver wootz steel blade, makara crossguard, and jade hilt; required for challenge and handover (Sc 4)

Agnivesh stops on the sand in front of Ranvijay's horse, just below the throne dais, closes his book, bends down and places it on the sandy ground. He rises, looks up towards Maharaja Someshwar on the dais and greets him with folded hands. For a split second, his right sleeve shifts up, revealing a faint golden SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist. He tugs the sleeve back down. AGNIVESH (steady, respectful) Pranaam Pitashri. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (hard, loud) HUH... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (feeling agony) Tujh jaise kaayar aur darpook insaan ko apna putra kahna .. aa thuuu.. ye mera aur poori praja ka apmaan hai.. Agnivesh straightens. The citizens are quiet now. AGNIVESH (low, controlled) Pitashri..Yeh mera bhi rajya hai aur main is rajya ka vaasi hu..mujhe bhi apna samarthya dikhaane ka mauka milna chahiye Agnivesh turns to his brother Ranvijay, places his right fist and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its sheath. His wrist mark flares beneath his sleeve, a jolt runs up his arm, and the sword slips from his hand and falls. everyone starts laughing loudly, Maharaja Someshwar also feeling the same. PRINCE RANVIJAY (laughing, sharp) ye tera rajya hai na?....to Ja aur rajya ke logo ka mal mootra saaf kar ke rajya ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar. kyunki tujh jaise insaan se yuddh karna to mere liye hi apmaan ki baat hai.. RAJGURU BADRINATH (arrogent, public) Rajkumar ek dam sahi kah rahe hain. Mrityu Grahan mein janma balak na to rajya ka varis ho skata hai aur na hi is pratiyogita me bhaag le sakta hai.., yahi niyam hai. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (murmuring, uneasy) Mrityu Grahan ... awwww.. kya ye sach hai? AGNIVESH (firm, restrained) janm se koi bhi apraadhi nahi hota raajguru, aur na hi janm lena koi apraadh hai. AGNIVESH (voice tight, respectful) Aapko poori praja ke saamne yun mera uphaas nahi karna chahiye maharaj. Maharaja Someshwar raises his hand. ① Theme, Premise & Narrative Core
Core Theme: Sovereign legitimacy is born from enduring sacrificial humiliation, not inherited thrones or martial arrogance.
Emotional Arc (Three Tiers):
Tier 1 (Martial Vaunt vs. Ascetic Quiet): Ranvijay projects broad, chest-forward pomp on horseback while Agnivesh maintains stillness, measured finger movements, and steady breathing over ancient manuscripts.
Tier 2 (The Crucible of Public Shaming): Physical escalation from standing defiance to kneeling in the arena sand with open, surrendered palms under imperial decree.
Tier 3 (Primordial Awakening): Complete stillness masking subterranean fury; the jaw locks, breathing suspends, and the dormant wrist seal ignites beneath scorched silk.
Audience Takeaway & Emotional Strategy: Cultivate acute cathartic anticipation. By driving filial rejection and brotherly arrogance to an unbearable peak, the audience is primed to crave ruthless karmic retribution, sealed by a supernatural physical cliffhanger.

② Visual Style & Framing Tone (16:9 Landscape with 9:16 Safe Area)
Compositional Grammar (16:9 Framing with Central 9:16 Safe Area):
Center-Weighted Safe Area Staging: The primary dramatic subjects, key physical blocking, eyelines, and critical micro-expressions are tightly locked within the central 9:16 vertical safe zone, ensuring full compositional integrity when cropped vertically for mobile microdrama platforms.
Horizontal Wings for Environmental Scale: The flanking left and right thirds of the 16:9 horizontal frame are dedicated to spatial scale—soaring sandstone colonnades, tiered spectator stands, billowing sun-mandala standards, and distant palace towers.
Vertical Stacking within Center Zone: Exploit the vertical depth of the central safe area to enforce hierarchy: Maharaja Someshwar commands the upper third on the elevated dais; Ranvijay commands the center third on horseback; Agnivesh occupies the lower third kneeling on the sand.
Frame-within-Frame: Use massive carved sandstone archways, gate thresholds, and marble pavilion pillars to enclose figures within the central safe area.
Three-Layer Spatial Depth:
Foreground: Ringing brass bridle bells, sand drifts, stone balustrades, or the ornate jade sword hilt placed close to the lens.
Midground: Primary actors executing smooth physical blocking—kneeling, mounting, drawing weapons, passing objects between open hands.
Background: Stacked spectator galleries, palace facades, and mountain waterfalls establishing monumental architecture.
Camera Movement & Dynamic Rhythm:
Camera Grammar: Exclusively smooth, controlled mechanical movements. Gliding dolly tracks, slow vertical crane pedestals, smooth jib arcs, and stable locked-off tripod shots.
Strict Exclusions: Zero handheld shake, zero whip-pans, zero crash zooms, and zero erratic camera jitter. Every motion begins and decelerates with silky, cinematic precision.
Dolly Push / Pull: Smooth, slow linear dolly push-ins to intensify psychological weight on crucial dialogue turns; smooth dolly pull-backs to reveal isolation against oppressive court grandeur.
Crane Pedestal: Vertical crane elevations tracking the power gradient between the high northern royal dais and the arena floor below.

④ Scene-by-Scene Emotion & Visual Intent
Scene 1: Royal Tournament Pavilion — The Arrogant Parade (Shots 1–6 / 45s)
Emotional Objective: Unchecked martial hubris; squared shoulders, lifted chin, smirking eye-locks.
Atmospheric Direction: Oppressive courtly pomp, intoxicating hubris, celebratory adulation.
Camera Intent: Smooth crane arm lowering from the high arena rim to an eye-level tracking dolly before the warhorse, capturing Ranvijay centered within the 9:16 safe area while the 16:9 wings capture cheering tiers.
Spatial Narrative: Ranvijay commands the central sand runway; Someshwar towers on the high northern throne dais.
Distance Design: Wide arena vista gliding smoothly into medium tracking of the stallion and close-up smirks.
Scene 2: Agnivesh's Reading Room — The Still Center (Shots 7–10 / 28s)
Emotional Objective: Deep meditative composure; slow turning of aged parchment; eyes tranquil despite distant roars.
Atmospheric Direction: Secluded gravitas, scholastic isolation.
Camera Intent: Slow linear dolly push-in toward Agnivesh seated in the window alcove, followed by a steady lateral slider tracking his deliberate stride toward the arched door.
Spatial Narrative: Claustrophobic stone interior framed by vertical shelves, insulating Agnivesh from the martial frenzy outside.
Distance Design: Macro detail of fingers on binding → Medium waist-level glide → Smooth follow shot to the threshold.
Scene 3: Royal Tournament Pavilion Entrance — The Scholar's Walk (Shots 11–12 / 14s)
Emotional Objective: Unshakable resolve stepping directly into hostility; steady, unhurried stride.
Atmospheric Direction: Imposing threshold, hostile public exposure.
Camera Intent: Symmetrical wide track positioned along the central corridor, following Agnivesh's back as the colossal gates smoothly part, gliding forward onto the bright sand threshold.
Spatial Narrative: Southern portal aligns directly on the cardinal axis facing the northern throne dais.
Distance Design: Wide threshold frame transitioning via forward dolly to a medium full-body profile.
Scene 4: Royal Tournament Pavilion — The Public Shaming & Blade Surrender (Shots 13–38 / 199s)
Emotional Objective: Venomous filial disgust from the king; cold gloating from Ranvijay; compressed righteous fury behind Agnivesh's locked jaw.
Atmospheric Direction: Visceral court tribunal, severe humiliation, supernatural dread.
Camera Intent:
Slow crane pedestal moving vertically between Someshwar's commanding downward gaze and Agnivesh's upright posture.
Smooth lateral slider passes tracking Ranvijay circling on the sand.
Stable locked-off medium close-ups on Rajguru's calculating smirk and Devika's unsmiling eyes.
Deliberate mechanical creep-in to the horizontal blade resting on open palms.
Slow, steady macro dolly toward Agnivesh's singeing cuff as the molten-gold brand activates.
Spatial Narrative: Triangular standoff: Someshwar elevated on the dais, Ranvijay standing over the sand, Agnivesh pinned on his knees between them.
Distance Design: Medium confrontation masters tightening systematically into intimate close-ups of eyes, clenched jaws, open hands, and radiant skin.

PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, smug) rakshak nahi rajguru ..main is rajya ka hone wala samraat hun aur ye praja meri daas... RAJMAHAL - DAY (CONTINUOUS) We see the sprawling view of a grand royal palace with endless rooms. INT. RAJMAHAL - AGNIVESH'S READING ROOM - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh A quiet room filled with bookshelves lined with ancient books. AGNIVESH (24, royal-blue angrakha, ivory dhoti, maroon angavastram, worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist) sits in shadow by a narrow window, slowly turning the pages of an ancient book. Hearing the distant roar from the arena, Agnivesh closes the book, rises and walks out through the hallway, book in hand. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Several Royal Courtiers, Several Citizens Citizens are cheering and making noise. In the courtiers' stand beside the throne dais, the Royal Courtiers sit chanting. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (chanting, mocking) Agnivesh! Agnivesh! Agnivesh CUT TO EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION ENTRANCE - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh We see a back view of Agnivesh walking toward the Grand Royal Arena with an ancient book in his hand as the massive royal door opens. Transitioning to a front entry view, Agnivesh steps through the grand entrance into the arena, holding the ancient book in hand and a worn ANCESTRAL SWORD hanging at his waist. EXT. ROYAL TOURNAMENT PAVILION - DAY (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Ranvijay's Horse, Maharaja Someshwar, Rajguru Badrinath, Devika, Royal Guard, Citizen, Several Citizens, Several Royal Courtiers Maharaja Someshwar sits on his throne on the dais, a ROYAL GUARD at attention beside him holding the tall royal sun banner. Rajguru Badrinath stands at the front rail of the courtiers' stand. Ranvijay is still on horseback in front of the stand. From his saddle, Ranvijay turns towards the south gate. AGNIVESH walks across the sand toward him, reading the book in his hand, the worn ANCESTRAL SWORD at his waist. PRINCE RANVIJAY (calling down, taunting, laughing) jise tum sab yuddh ke liye bula rahe ho vo koi yoddha nahi balki ek durbal aur kaayar naari ke samaan hai.... Rajguru Badrinath turns from the courtiers' stand toward the Maharaja on the dais. RAJGURU BADRINATH (soft, poisonous) kaayaron ko yuddh se door hi rakhna chahiye maharaj. Main aapse anurodh karta hun Yuvraj Ranvijay ko is rajya ka hone wala samraat ghoshit kiya jaaye. The citizens laugh at him and whisper to each other. A CITIZEN leaning over the railing of the stone stands calls out. CITIZEN (mocking) haar ke dar se.. haath mein kitaab leke aaya hai... Agnivesh stops on the sand in front of Ranvijay's horse, just below the throne dais, closes his book, bends down and places it on the sandy ground. He rises, looks up towards Maharaja Someshwar on the dais and greets him with folded hands. For a split second, his right sleeve shifts up, revealing a faint golden SWORD-SHAPED MARK on his wrist. He tugs the sleeve back down. AGNIVESH (steady, respectful) Pranaam Pitashri. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (hard, loud) HUH... MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (feeling agony) Tujh jaise kaayar aur darpook insaan ko apna putra kahna .. aa thuuu.. ye mera aur poori praja ka apmaan hai.. Agnivesh straightens. The citizens are quiet now. AGNIVESH (low, controlled) Pitashri..Yeh mera bhi rajya hai aur main is rajya ka vaasi hu..mujhe bhi apna samarthya dikhaane ka mauka milna chahiye Agnivesh turns to his brother Ranvijay, places his right fist and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its sheath. His wrist mark flares beneath his sleeve, a jolt runs up his arm, and the sword slips from his hand and falls. everyone starts laughing loudly, Maharaja Someshwar also feeling the same. PRINCE RANVIJAY (laughing, sharp) ye tera rajya hai na?....to Ja aur rajya ke logo ka mal mootra saaf kar ke rajya ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar. kyunki tujh jaise insaan se yuddh karna to mere liye hi apmaan ki baat hai.. RAJGURU BADRINATH (arrogent, public) Rajkumar ek dam sahi kah rahe hain. Mrityu Grahan mein janma balak na to rajya ka varis ho skata hai aur na hi is pratiyogita me bhaag le sakta hai.., yahi niyam hai. SEVERAL ROYAL COURTIERS (murmuring, uneasy) Mrityu Grahan ... awwww.. kya ye sach hai? AGNIVESH (firm, restrained) janm se koi bhi apraadhi nahi hota raajguru, aur na hi janm lena koi apraadh hai. Agnivesh looks towards Maharaja Someshwar Maharaja Someshwar rises from his throne in anger, towering over Agnivesh from the dais. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, cutting) Tu janm lete hi apni maa ko nigal gya .. yahi tera sabse bada apraadh hai. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (louder, cruelly formal) Tujhe is Rajmahal aur is rajya mein bas teri mari hui maa aur meri kripa ki wajah se rahne diya gaya hai. Agnivesh falls down on his knees just right besides the Ancestor Sword, he joins his hands and starts pleading to his father Maharaja Someshwar. AGNIVESH (voice tight, respectful) Aapko poori praja ke saamne yun mera uphaas nahi karna chahiye maharaj. Maharaja Someshwar raises his hand. The ROYAL GUARD beside the throne lowers the royal sun banner. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (commanding, public) main Iss rajya ka Maharaj, tujhe ye aadesh deta hun...ki tu apni maa ki ye mahaan talwaar abhi Ranvijay ko saunp de. ye talwaar ek sacche rajkumaar ke haath mein hi shobha deti hai naaki tujh jaise kaayar aur shraapit insaan ke... Agnivesh picks up his sword, gets up and grips the hilt. SEVERAL CITIZENS (cheering, loud) Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Yuvraj Ranvijay ki jai! Ranvijay steps down from his horse, walks towards Agnivesh and holds out his palm without looking at Agnivesh. PRINCE RANVIJAY (quiet, arrogant) Ye talwaar mujhe de de Agnivesh.. AGNIVESH (voice deep, controlled) Ye talwaar tumhe sweekar hi nahi karegi..kyuki tum iske laayak hi nahi ho. In fear that a fight might break out between the two, the people standing around start breaking out in a nervous sweat. Everybody looking at Ranvijay’s open palm. Maharaja Someshwar steps forward to the edge of the dais and points his finger at Agnivesh. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (anger , shouting) Agnivesh........... Talwar Ranvijay ko saunp do anyatha tumhe abhi mrityu dand diya jaayega.. A pause. Someshwar surveys the whole arena. MAHARAJA SOMESHWAR (cold, final) Ab koi pratiyogita nahi hogi.kyuki tum pratiyogita ke kaabil hi nahi ho. yahi hamara antim nirnay hai. Agnivesh slowly raises the ANCESTRAL SWORD, holds it upright before his chest, then lays it across Ranvijay’s waiting palms. Ranvijay closes his fingers around the sword. He raises it for the court. PRINCE RANVIJAY (triumphant, loud) aakhirkar is talwaar ko apna asli maalik mil hi gaya.. The citizens and royal courtiers laugh at Agnivesh. Among the laughing courtiers in the stand behind the Rajguru, one does not smile: DEVIKA (22, turquoise-and-gold warrior attire, a short curved dagger at her belt), the Rajguru's niece. Her eyes stay on Agnivesh. Agnivesh lowers his empty hand. CLOSE ON his right wrist: his sleeve slides back, revealing the SWORD-SHAPED MARK burning molten gold, its heat scorching the silk cuff. HARD CUT

An ancient CELESTIAL WARD MAP lies open on a carved wooden table, projecting a glowing, translucent 3D hologram of seven majestic gates of light surrounding the realm. DEVIKA (22, turquoise-and-gold warrior attire, a short curved dagger at her belt) turns a brass compass above the map. AGNIVESH, still in his full-sleeved royal-blue silk angrakha, ivory dhoti and maroon angavastram, his right cuff faintly scorched, studies the hologram intently. Within it, the northern sun-seal flickers violet and pulses weakly. The doors BURST OPEN. RANVIJAY strides in, Agnivesh's mother's ANCESTRAL SWORD thrust through his waist sash like a trophy, his own curved talwar in its dark-red scabbard at his left hip. Two royal guards follow and halt just inside the doorway. PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, mocking) Main hoon is rajya ka hone wala Maharaj. Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh with a smirking grin, resting his hand casually on the hilt of the ANCESTRAL SWORD. PRINCE RANVIJAY (loud, mocking) Mujhe dekhte hi tum sabka mastak mere sammaan mein jhuk jaana chahiye... Agnivesh looks up, unbothered. AGNIVESH (steady, low) Yuddh kiye bina hi khud ko vijeta ghoshit karne waale ko Maharaj nahi, kapti kaha jaata hai. Ranvijay steps toward the table. PRINCE RANVIJAY (rising, cruel) Jo khud apni maa ko maar daale, usse bada hatyara aur koi nahi ho sakta. Agnivesh's right fist closes behind his back. His left hand grips the right sleeve over his wrist; a faint golden glow pulses through the silk, then fades. Devika notices the northern sun-seal on the CELESTIAL WARD MAP flicker violet and pulse weakly. DEVIKA (rapid, urgent) Yuvraj Ranvijay... rajya ka suraksha tantra kamzor ho raha hai.. hamein abhi kuch karna hoga.. PRINCE RANVIJAY (dismissive, loud) Yeh naksha sab kuch galat dikha raha hai. Hamara rajya poori tarah surakshit hai. Devika points to the map. DEVIKA (sharp, controlled) Dhyaan se dekhiye, Yuvraj.. hamari seema-rekha par saat pracheen Raksha-Dwaar hain. Ek bhi gira toh samundar se... Prince Ranvijay walks around the table to Devika and places his finger on her lips. PRINCE RANVIJAY (leering, low) Sssshhh... tum bahut bolti ho. Main tumhare hothon ko band karne ke upaay bhi jaanta hoon... Agnivesh strides to Ranvijay and shoves him away from Devika. AGNIVESH (level, cutting) Dhikkar hai tum par, Ranvijay! Rajya khatre mein hai aur tum Devika par apni hawas ka jaal faila rahe ho. Ranvijay grips the hilt of the ANCESTRAL SWORD in fury and advances on Agnivesh. PRINCE RANVIJAY (low, threatening) Ek raja ko dhakka dene ki himmat kaise hui teri? Tu hota kaun hai mujhe batane wala? Tu mere baap ki rakhail ka ladka hai... naajaayaz hai tu. Naajaayaz! AGNIVESH (steady, direct) Tumhe Devika ke hothon ke baare mein nahi... rajya ke baare mein sochna chahiye. PRINCE RANVIJAY (angry) Rakshako! The two royal guards draw their swords and stride in from the doorway to stand beside Ranvijay. ROYAL GUARD 1 (firm, resolute) Aadesh Yuvraj. Agnivesh and Ranvijay stand face to face, glaring. Devika steps between them and pushes them apart. DEVIKA (quiet, pointed) Aap dono ko yahan nahi, yuddh-bhoomi mein ladna chahiye. Kyunki jab seema ke dwaar tootenge, tabhi yoddha ki asli pehchaan hogi. Devika presses her palm onto the CELESTIAL WARD MAP. The hologram collapses back into it, and the map shrinks into a single sheet of ancient parchment. She folds it carefully, picks up her brass compass and walks out through the stone archway at the back of the archive. INT. ARCHIVE WARD CORRIDOR - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 A tense procession moves through the torch-lit corridor. Devika leads, holding the folded map and brass compass, with Agnivesh close behind. Ranvijay follows, the sheathed ANCESTRAL SWORD now in his hand, dragging its scabbard tip along the floor and scraping streaks into the stone. The two royal guards bring up the rear. INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) Characters: Agnivesh, Prince Ranvijay, Devika, Royal Guard 1, Royal Guard 2 Devika carries the map into the inner chamber. Agnivesh and Ranvijay follow. The two royal guards take position on either side of the chamber door. A SUN-SEAL RELIC, a round golden disc with concentric rings, is set into the centre of the stone floor. Devika kneels at the relic and unrolls the map over it; Agnivesh kneels opposite her and helps press it flat. Ranvijay stands back near the door, arms folded. The relic's golden rings begin to turn. Seven sun-marks rise from the map, and a glowing 3D hologram of SWARNADWEEP blooms above the floor: the island with the city of Suryagarh at its heart, ringed by sea and by seven enormous gates of light rising from the water. Golden beams link the seven gates into a protective dome over the whole realm. Devika spreads her hands. The hologram grows until it surrounds all three of them, the island before them and the ocean all around. At Devika's gesture, the northern gate's doors open, and a bright current of seawater rushes toward the island. A violet crack splits the gate's doors. They jam. The water turns black, and dark mist curls through the opening toward Swarnadweep. The dome beside the northern gate goes dark while the other six gates stay lit. Devika's brass compass spins wildly. The hologram shakes, breaks into streams of golden light and collapses into the Sun-Seal Relic. On the map, the northern gate's symbol keeps flickering violet. DEVIKA (fast, alarmed) Dwaar ki shakti toot rahi hai. Yeh kisi ki saazish hai. Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai.. PRINCE RANVIJAY (flat, dismissive) Bas karo yeh dhong. Har parchhai mein tum dono ko gaddaar aur raakshas hi dikhte hain. AGNIVESH (deep, controlled) Raakshas tab aate hain jab rajkumar shatru se ladne ke bajaay, apnon ki gardan par hi talwaar rakh de. PRINCE RANVIJAY (furious, rising) Tu mujhe kamzor keh raha hai? AGNIVESH (firm, unblinking) Nahi. Main tumhe darpok keh raha hoon. The two guards close in on either side of Agnivesh. Devika steps beside the ward relic. Ranvijay strides up to Agnivesh beside the relic and draws the ANCESTRAL SWORD from its scabbard. CLOSE ON the blade's edge at Agnivesh's throat, his calm eyes above it. PRINCE RANVIJAY (low, shaking with rage) Ek aur shabd, aur meri ye talwaar tera sir dhadd se alag kar degi. Devika raises one palm between them but does not touch the blade. DEVIKA (hard, urgent) Ranvijay, talwaar neeche karo. PRINCE RANVIJAY (snapping) Chup reh! Tu hoti kaun hai hamare beech mein bolne wali? Kahin tu bhi iski rakhail to nahi... bilkul iski maa ki tarah? Agnivesh steps forward. The blade nicks his skin. A thin line of blood appears. AGNIVESH (low, clear) Jo maarna jaante hain, vo baatein nahi karte.. aur tere toh haath hi kaanp rahe hain, mere bhai. Ranvijay’s wrist trembles. The ANCESTRAL SWORD shakes before every guard. PRINCE RANVIJAY (strained, shouting) Main kisi se nahi darta! Agnivesh raises a single finger to the blade at his throat. His right sleeve slides back: the SWORD-SHAPED MARK glows gold, and the sunstone on the ANCESTRAL SWORD's guard flickers in answer. With one finger, he presses the blade away from his neck. The sword swings down out of Ranvijay's control; he stumbles back a step in shock. The guards stare in disbelief. AGNIVESH (calm, cutting) Talwaar pakadne se koi yoddha nahi ban jaata. Ranvijay charges at Agnivesh with the ANCESTRAL SWORD raised. Behind them, the scorched northern gate symbol on the map flashes violet. Every torch in the chamber gutters at once. Ranvijay freezes mid-stride. CLOSE ON the violet symbol pulsing in the dark. HARD CUT

## Director Production Plan: Episode 2 — Khatre ka Sanket

① Theme & Narrative Core

Core Theme: Sovereign authority is earned through internal mastery and duty to the realm. It is never inherited through arrogant entitlement or enforced by blunt terror.

Emotional Spine:

Tier 1 (Suppressed Endurance): Agnivesh keeps his burning mark hidden beneath scorched silk. He takes Ranvijay's insults with a still posture and steady breathing, and keeps his focus on the realm's defence.
Tier 2 (Moral Intervention): The taunts turn physical when Ranvijay touches Devika's lips. Agnivesh breaks his stillness with an immediate, forceful shove and takes moral command of the room.
Tier 3 (Absolute Dominance & Reversal): With the Ancestral Sword at his throat, Agnivesh steps into the blade. As his mark glows and the sword's sunstone answers, he presses the trembling steel away with one bare finger. Ranvijay stumbles back, charges in rage, and freezes mid-stride as the northern symbol flashes violet and every torch gutters.

Exit Takeaway & Expression Strategy: Immediate catharsis as the scorned half-brother shatters the crown prince's show of bravery without ever holding a weapon. It is followed at once by looming jeopardy as the northern ward fails, ending on a hard cut.

Natural Acting Direction (all scenes)
Grounded and real: Every performance is understated and believable, played as if no camera were there. There are no theatrical poses, no stage gestures and no mugging to the lens.
Eyes and micro-expressions over big gestures:
Emotion reads through the eyes, breath, the jaw and small shifts of weight.
Examples: a held breath, a blink when the blade nicks, a glance that lands and leaves, a fist closing out of sight.
Dialogue:
Spoken at a natural conversational pace, verbatim, never declaimed.
Pauses come from thought, not from the camera.
Lines land on the listener's face as often as on the speaker's.
Where intensity rises:
Only for the villain, Ranvijay, and for extreme emotion: Devika's alarm at the breach, Ranvijay's rage and fear at the blade, the charge and the freeze.
Even then it stays believable. Ranvijay's bluster sits over real insecurity, his trembling hand is real fear, and his rage is a man losing control, not a performance of anger.
Stillness as power: Agnivesh is the stillest person in every frame. The less he moves, the more he commands, so the shove and the single finger land as events.
Listening: Every character is alive when not speaking, reacting in real time. The guards are disciplined and impassive until the finger beat breaks their composure.
② Visual Style & Framing Tone (Native 9:16 Vertical)

Vertical Composition Rules:

Native 9:16: Every shot is composed for 9:16 vertical, with all characters fully inside frame. Every camera note ends with "9:16 vertical composition, all characters fully inside frame".
Two side by side at most: Groups of three or more are stacked in depth (foreground, midground, background), never in a horizontal line.
Centre third: Faces, eyelines and key hands (the finger on the blade, the palm on the map, the trembling wrist) stay in the centre vertical third.
Using height:
An aerial drift over the palace domes in the time-lapse (1).
A crane down from the archive vault onto the glowing table (2).
Low angles on Ranvijay's bluster and fear (9, 39, 41) and on Agnivesh's answers and rebukes (5, 13, 33, 44).
Overheads on the map and the circle of men (19, 35, 46), and a high crane as they kneel at the relic (24).
A low angle from the map looking up at Devika and Agnivesh, her face in the top third and his in the bottom third (25).
A tilt and crane up into the hologram dome (26), and a tilt down from the darkened dome to the spinning compass (29).
A crane up as Agnivesh rises from his knee (33).

Composition Style & Narrative Rationale:

Framing-Within-Framing:
The archive's bookshelves and stone archway, the corridor's stone walls and pillars, and the chamber doorway and dome ribs box in Ranvijay and his guards.
This visually marks their moral limits and trapped arrogance.
Symmetry vs. Diagonal Conflict:
Symmetry is held during the ritual reading of the Celestial Ward Map, to show ancestral order.
It breaks into diagonals whenever Ranvijay crosses the space to disrupt it.
Screen Line (continues Ep 1): Ranvijay is always screen-left, facing right. Agnivesh and Devika are screen-right, facing left.

Three-Layer Spatial Separation:

Foreground: Physical barriers: carved table corners, hovering hologram light, the relic's rings, sword hilts.
Midground: The principal players (Agnivesh, Ranvijay, Devika) locked in confrontation.
Background: Deep perspective of the stone vaults, library stacks, guarded doorways and the dome. Guards sit here, stacked in depth.
Cinematography Direction

Camera Movement (mostly motivated, flowing moves):

Flowing (39 of 46 shots): Smooth movement, always motivated by a character's move, a look or a reveal:
slow dolly track-in and track-out;
arcs and circular tracks (around Ranvijay's strut, the hologram table and the relic);
tilts and crane moves for height;
one gentle aerial drift-in for the palace time-lapse (1).
Fast beats (exactly five in the episode):
The doors bursting open (3, snap push-in).
Agnivesh's shove (12, handheld-energy push).
The blade to the throat (36, snap push-in).
Ranvijay's charge (45, fast track that stops dead on the freeze).
The violet symbol (46, crash zoom that stops on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol in frame).
Static holds (two, for emphasis): Agnivesh's calm lines "Tumhe Devika ke hothon…" (16) and "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
No whip-pans, no jump cuts, no crash cuts. No two consecutive shots share the same size and angle.

Shot-Size Variety:

Extreme wide: The palace time-lapse (1).
Wides: The archive and chamber masters (2, 10, 17, 23, 24, 27, 30), the corridor procession (21), the overhead circle (35) and the charge (45).
Full shot: The profile two-shot of both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat (37).
Medium wides and mediums: Carry the confrontations.
Medium close-ups: For the insults and rebukes, and the reaction two-shot of Devika and Agnivesh from the map (25).
Close-ups, extreme close-ups and inserts: Kept for the fist and sleeve (7), the palm on the map (19), the scabbard tip (22), the blade at the throat (36), the finger, mark and sunstone (42) and the violet symbol (46, a top-down close-up framed with a dark margin so nothing crops).
Over-the-shoulder pairs (5–6, 15, 34) and the profile two-shot (37) keep both brothers in every exchange.

Lens Choices & Depth of Field (matching the location plates' full-frame anamorphic look):

Wide and establishing: 24–32mm equivalent, with deep focus so groups stacked in depth all read (for example the procession in 21 and the guards behind Ranvijay in 17).
Mediums and two-shots: 40–50mm, with moderate depth: the speaker sharp and the background readable but soft.
Medium close-ups and close-ups: 75–85mm, with shallow depth of field. In the over-the-shoulder shots the near shoulder is soft and the far face sharp, with Devika soft in the background of 13.
Inserts: 100mm macro on the fist, the blade, the finger and the symbol, with a very shallow focal plane.
Rack focus:
Rack from Agnivesh to Devika in the reaction two-shot over the map (25).
Rack from the blade edge to Agnivesh's eyes (36, 40).
Rack from the raised finger to the glowing mark and sunstone (42).
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture, real fabric and metal, and a subtle anamorphic flare only from real light sources. No CGI look, no plastic skin.
③ Narrative Structure & Pacing (46 Shots / 262 Seconds)

Narrative Model: Full narrative arc for a high-velocity vertical microdrama. 46 shots, 262 seconds, averaging about 5.7 seconds per shot. Dialogue is never rushed.

Paragraph Division Table:

No.	Sequence Name	Scene	Shots	Duration	Core Event	Emotional Intensity	Tempo
P1	The Imperial Sentinel	Sc 1	1	4s	Time-lapse: day to moonlit night over Suryagarh palace	30%	Fluid, compressed
P2	Darbar of Insolence	Sc 2	2–20	117s	The northern seal flickers; Ranvijay bursts in, insults Agnivesh and touches Devika; Agnivesh shoves him; guards summoned; Devika parts them and collapses the map	70%	Combative, with flowing coverage
P3	The Tense Transit	Sc 3	21–22	9s	Procession through the corridor; the Ancestral Sword's scabbard tip scrapes the stone	55%	Heavy, suspenseful
P4	Fracture & Defiance	Sc 4	23–46	132s	The ward ritual shows the northern gate breached; Ranvijay draws steel; Agnivesh pushes it away with one finger; the charge; the torches gutter; Ranvijay freezes; hard cut on the violet symbol	98%	Building to explosive cliffhanger
Total	Full Episode	4 scenes	46	262s			

Video Tracks (12):

Track	Shots	Duration	Scene(s)
1	1–4	23s	Rajmahal Exterior, Royal Archives
2	5–8	23s	Royal Archives

Emotional Curve:

It opens at dynastic scale as the day dies over the palace (Sc 1).
It accelerates into court aggression (Sc 2) and tightens along the narrow corridor (Sc 3).
It peaks in a lethal standoff and cosmic breach (Sc 4), ending on a hard cut.

Key Visual Turning Points (No Dialogue Reliance):

The Physical Push: Agnivesh breaks his passive posture and shoves Ranvijay away from Devika (12).
The Holographic Breach: A violet crack splits the northern gate, the seawater turns black and that part of the dome goes dark (28–29).
The Finger Deflection: Ranvijay's wrist trembles. Agnivesh's bare finger presses the blade away while his mark glows and the sunstone answers (41–43).
The Torch Gutter:
The northern symbol flashes violet and every torch gutters at once.
Ranvijay freezes mid-charge (45).
Crash zoom on the pulsing violet symbol, then HARD CUT (46).
Pacing Direction (beat by beat)

Principle: Breathe where the story is thinking, accelerate where it is acting. Every insult gets a beat of reaction before the answer. The five fast beats are the only places the cut rate and camera speed jump, and each is followed by a slower shot so it lands.

Sc 1 (1, 4s), breathe: One unhurried establishing image. Let the night arrive fully before cutting.

Sc 2 (2–20, 117s), build in waves:

2 (7s), breathe: The slow crane down lets the audience read the seven gates and the violet flicker before anyone speaks.
3 (6s), accelerate: The doors burst open (fast beat 1). The first jolt.
4–6 (6s, 7s, 6s), steady volley: Strut, answer, accusation. Even rhythm. Hold one beat on Agnivesh's face after "kapti" before cutting to Ranvijay.
7 (4s), reaction hold: The fist and the glow through the sleeve. A silent beat that tells the audience what he is holding back.
8–10 (6s, 6s, 7s), urgency: Devika's warning, Ranvijay's dismissal, the arc around the table. Cut 10 on the interruption, at "samundar se...".
11 (8s), slow menace: Let the finger on the lips play long and uncomfortable. Hold on Devika's frozen eyes.
12 (4s), accelerate: The shove (fast beat 2).
13–15 (8s, 7s, 5s), escalate: The rebuke, the advance, "naajaayaz". Cuts get shorter as Ranvijay loses control.
16 (6s), stillness: A static hold on Agnivesh's reply. The scene's eye of the storm.
17 (6s), threat: The guards draw.
18 (9s), longest breath of the scene: Devika's line, with the brothers' reactions held behind her.
19–20 (4s, 5s), release: The map collapses and Devika walks away, letting the air out before the corridor.

Sc 3 (21–22, 9s), heavy rhythm: Measured, silent, the scrape of the scabbard as the metronome. No dialogue, no rush.

Sc 4 (23–46, 132s), wonder, dread, standoff, explosion:

23–24 (5s, 5s), settle: The entry and kneeling. Calm before the ritual.
25 (5s), breathe: The reaction over the map. Let the audience read Devika's quiet hope and Agnivesh's unease in their eyes before the relic wakes. No dialogue, no rush.
26–29 (6s, 5s, 6s, 4s), wonder turning to dread: The bloom, the hologram surrounding them, the breach, the spinning compass. The cut rate quickens slightly as the gate fails.
30 (5s), collapse: The hologram streams into the relic. A beat of silence before anyone speaks.
31–34 (6s, 6s, 7s, 7s), argument: Devika's alarm, with her glance held on "Gaddaar…". Ranvijay's dismissal, Agnivesh rising, "kamzor / darpok". Let each line land on the listener.
35 (4s), tension: The guards close in. Silent.
36 (5s), accelerate: The blade to the throat (fast beat 3).
37–39 (5s, 4s, 9s), pressure: The threat, Devika's palm, Ranvijay's tirade. Hold the full 9s on the tirade so his loss of control shows.
40 (9s), slowest beat of the episode: Agnivesh steps into the blade. Give the nick and the line their full time.
41 (4s), crack: "Main kisi se nahi darta!". Short and strained.
42 (6s), silence: The finger, the mark and the sunstone. Hold it in the silence.
43 (5s), reaction hold: The sword swings down. Hold on the guards' disbelief and Ranvijay's shock.
44 (4s), stillness: A static hold on "Talwaar pakadne se…".
45 (6s), accelerate: The charge (fast beat 4). The torches gutter and he freezes. Stop dead.
46 (4s), crash zoom, then HARD CUT: The crash zoom (fast beat 5), the violet pulse, then HARD CUT on the pulse. No lingering, no fade.
④ Scene-by-Scene Emotion & Camera Intent
Scene 1: EXT. RAJMAHAL - DAY TO NIGHT (TIME-LAPSE) (Shot 1 / 4s)
Emotional Target: The weight of the institution; night closing in after the events of Ep 1.
Atmosphere Direction: Monumental, grand, ominous.
Camera Intent: An extreme-wide time-lapse with a gentle aerial drift-in toward the main dome. The sun races across the sky, the shadows sweep, and a bright full moon rises over the domes. The drift stays small so the day first frame and the moonlit last frame line up.
Spatial Staging & Distance: The palace domes sit in the middle third, with the sky and moon in the top third and the terraces and valley mist in the bottom third.
Acting Notes: No characters.
Lighting Plan:
Start on the Rajmahal Exterior plate's golden daylight, with clear sky and long shadows.
Move through a short amber dusk as the windows light up one by one with oil lamps.
End on the Moonlit Night plate: a deep-indigo starry sky, the full moon just above the main dome, a silver moonlight rim on the domes, lamp-lit windows and valley mist.
Scene 2: INT. ROYAL ARCHIVES - NIGHT (Shots 2–20 / 117s)
Emotional Target: Toxic provocation met with icy moral defiance.
Atmosphere Direction: Claustrophobic, hostile, volatile.
Camera Intent:
Opening: A slow crane down from the vault onto the glowing seven-gate hologram, with Devika turning the compass and Agnivesh leaning in (2).
The entrance: The doors burst open on a snap push-in (fast beat 1, 3). Ranvijay struts around Agnivesh on a slow circular track (4).
The insults:
Over-the-shoulder shots and dolly-ins carry the insults (5, 6, 13, 15).
A low-angle tilt up on Ranvijay waving the map away (9).
A slow tilt down finds Agnivesh's fist and the glow through his sleeve (7).
A slow track-out ahead of Ranvijay as he grips the hilt and advances toward the lens, so he grows in frame and the move ends behind Agnivesh's shoulder for the over-the-shoulder (14).
Devika: A crane down from the violet seal to Devika (8), then a high arc around the table as she points to the gates (10).
The lips: A track with Ranvijay up the left side into a profile two-shot of his finger on Devika's lips (11).
The shove: A handheld-energy push (fast beat 2, 12).
The guards: Agnivesh's reply is a static hold (16). The guards are summoned on a high crane-back (17).
Devika parts them: A low-angle push-in as Devika parts the brothers (18). A top-down crane as the hologram collapses into the map (19). A tilt up as she folds it and walks out through the archway (20).
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The table runs from the double doors at the near end to the shelves and stone archway at the far end.
Devika stands at the far end facing the doors. Agnivesh is at the table's right side.
Ranvijay enters from the doors, circles behind Agnivesh to the near end, then walks up the left side to Devika.
The guards halt just inside the doorway, then draw and stride up to stand behind Ranvijay.
Devika sets her compass on the table before pushing the brothers apart. The brothers step back into the top third, one either side of her.
Acting Notes:
Agnivesh:
Absorbed in the map; he does not look up when the doors crash open.
He answers without raising his voice. The only tells are a set jaw, a slow breath and the fist closing behind his back.
On the finger on Devika's lips, a flash in the eyes, then decisive action. The shove is functional, not theatrical.
Afterwards he is completely still again. The rebuke is level and cutting, not shouted.
Devika:
Focused and professional over the map. She notices the flicker with a small, real frown, and her urgency is controlled.
When Ranvijay touches her lips, she goes still with cold eyes: no flinch, no melodrama.
She parts the brothers with a firm, economical push, and her line is quiet and pointed.
Ranvijay:
The villain, allowed more size. A swaggering strut and a smirk; he enjoys his audience, loud and mocking.
The insults carry real venom.
After the shove, the humiliation flushes into rage, with his hand going to the hilt. It stays a petulant prince, not a cartoon.
Royal Guards: Impassive and disciplined. "Aadesh Yuvraj" is clipped and dutiful, and they draw in unison.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Royal Archives plate: brass oil lamps and wall torches as the warm, flickering key, with deep moody shadows and floating dust in the shafts of light.
The hologram: A motivated soft gold source from table height, uplighting Devika's and Agnivesh's faces and catching the brass instruments.
The violet flicker: The flickering northern seal throws a faint violet pulse onto Devika's face (2, 8).
The doors: The burst sends a draught that makes the torch flames flare and shadows jump (3).
The collapse: When the hologram collapses (19), the gold fill drops away and the faces fall back to lamp and torchlight only.
Faces: Lit by the same flicker and colour temperature as the set, with real contact shadows on the table and floor.
Scene 3: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CORRIDOR - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 21–22 / 9s)
Emotional Target: Simmering hatred, rhythmic threat.
Atmosphere Direction: Heavy, echoing, claustrophobic.
Camera Intent:
A slow track backward ahead of the procession (21).
Then a low track alongside the scabbard tip of the sheathed Ancestral Sword grinding the stone, tilting up to Ranvijay's sullen face (22).
Spatial Staging & Distance: Single file toward the camera, stacked in depth: Devika (folded map and compass), Agnivesh, Ranvijay (sword in his right hand), then the two guards together.
Acting Notes:
Devika: Brisk and purposeful, eyes ahead.
Agnivesh: Calm, eyes forward, ignoring the scraping behind him.
Ranvijay: Sullen. The drag is a deliberate, petulant provocation, with a small sneer.
Guards: Eyes ahead.
Lighting Plan:
Match the Archive Ward Corridor plate: wall torches in iron brackets and light haze.
Warm pools of torchlight alternate with deep shadow, so light rolls across each face as they pass each torch.
Sparks of light catch on the scabbard tip.
Scene 4: INT. ARCHIVE WARD CHAMBER - NIGHT (CONTINUOUS) (Shots 23–46 / 132s)
Emotional Target: Desperate alarm giving way to absolute sovereign dominance, ending in catastrophic dread.
Atmosphere Direction: Ritualistic, electric, terrifying.
Camera Intent:
The entry (23): A slow track back as they enter. Ranvijay slides the sword back into his sash.
The ritual (24–29):
A high crane as Devika and Agnivesh kneel at the relic and its rings turn (24).
The reaction (25): A two-shot from the map looking up, Devika's face in the top third and Agnivesh's in the bottom third, lit gold from below by the turning relic rings with the dark dome between them. A slow push-in with a gentle rack focus from Agnivesh to Devika.
A low tilt and crane up as the hologram blooms into the dome (26).
A circular track inside the growing hologram (27).
A push-in on the northern gate as it opens and breaches (28).
A tilt down to the spinning compass (29).
The collapse (30): A crane down as the hologram streams into the relic.
The argument (31–34): A low-angle push-in as Devika rises (31) and a low crane up as Agnivesh rises (33). A dolly-in on Ranvijay by the door (32). An over-the-shoulder arc for "kamzor / darpok" (34).
The draw (35–36): An overhead as the guards close in (35). The draw, with a snap push-in to the blade at the throat (fast beat 3, 36).
The blade at the throat (37–41):
A full-shot profile two-shot, both brothers head to toe, the blade a level line at Agnivesh's throat and the dome above, on a slow push-in (37).
A slow crane down past the blade in the foreground to Devika's raised palm and face (38).
A slow arc around Ranvijay for the tirade (39).
A slow push-in as Agnivesh steps into the blade and the nick appears (40).
A low-angle medium wide on Ranvijay's trembling sword arm, the guards watching from behind in depth, on a slow tilt up (41).
The finger (42–44): Starting close on the finger on the blade and the glowing wrist mark, a slow arc track-out reveals his calm face and the sunstone (42). A track-out as the sword swings down and Ranvijay stumbles (43). A static low angle on "Talwaar pakadne se…" (44).
The ending (45–46): A fast track on the charge, stopping dead as the torches gutter (fast beat 4, 45). A crash zoom down onto the violet symbol, stopping on a top-down close-up with the whole symbol inside frame and a margin of dark parchment around it (fast beat 5, 46), then HARD CUT.
Spatial Staging & Distance:
The relic is at the centre. The door is on the west side (screen-left), with the guards on either side of it.
Devika kneels on the relic's far side, facing the camera. Agnivesh kneels on the near side.
Ranvijay waits by the door, arms folded.
On "Gaddaar hamare beech mein hi hai", Devika glances toward Ranvijay.
The guards close in on either side of Agnivesh before the draw, and stay a pace behind him.
The shots tighten from the full chamber to the macro of blade and skin, then open out as Ranvijay stumbles back.
Acting Notes:
Devika:
Over the map before the bloom (25): focused and quietly hopeful as she searches it. Eyes, breath and a slight lean only.
Quiet awe as the hologram blooms. Then dread: her eyes track the failing gate and her breath catches.
She rises fast and alarmed, but grounded.
The glance at Ranvijay on "Gaddaar…" is a quick sideways look that lands and leaves, not a stare.
Her raised palm is steady, and her voice is firm, not pleading.
Agnivesh:
Over the map (25): his brow tightens with unease. No gesture, just the eyes and a held breath.
Calm and controlled. He rises without hurry and answers deep and level.
He steps into the blade without bravado, eyes on Ranvijay's eyes. The nick registers only as a blink.
The finger rises slowly and with certainty. "Talwaar pakadne se…" is almost quiet.
Ranvijay:
Dismissive with folded arms, then wounded pride at "darpok".
The draw is fast and real. The threat is low and shaking.
Real fear sits under the rage: the trembling wrist, a swallow, eyes flicking to the guards.
"Main kisi se nahi darta!" is strained, close to cracking.
The stumble is genuine shock. The charge is full rage.
The freeze is sudden fear: his eyes widen and his breath stops.
Royal Guards:
Impassive as they close in.
At the finger, a shared glance of disbelief and half a step back.
Lighting Plan:
Base light: Match the Archive Ward Chamber plate: warm amber torches as the key, a cool blue-violet moonlight rim, the relic's soft gold glow from below, mystical haze and deep shadow at the edges.
The ritual:
The reaction over the map (25): both faces lit gold from below by the turning relic rings, with the dome dark above them.
The blooming hologram fills the dome with motivated gold light that wraps the kneeling figures (26–27).
At the breach the northern gate turns violet-black, throwing cold violet onto Devika's face, and that sector of the dome goes dark (28–29).
After the collapse (30) the light returns to torches and the relic.
The finger: The mark's gold glow and the sunstone flicker act as small practical sources, lighting the finger and the blade (42).
The ending:
The map symbol flashes violet. Every torch gutters at once to red embers and smoke (45).
From then on, the violet glow is the only light: hard, cold, from below, catching only Ranvijay's raised blade and eyes.
Then the hard cut (46).
Integration: Skin, metal and fabric take the same flicker, colour and direction as the plate (warm amber on the breastplate and the sword, gold uplight from the relic), with real contact shadows on the stone floor.
Lighting Direction (all scenes)
Match the plate: Every shot is lit to match its location asset's lighting: the same direction, colour temperature, contrast and haze.
Integrated characters: Characters are lit by the set's own sources, never by a separate flat key, so they never look pasted-on. Contact shadows, bounce and flicker must agree with the plate.
Period-correct sources only: Oil lamps, torches, moonlight and daylight. The hologram, the relic, the mark and the violet symbol are treated as motivated light sources (gold or violet) that spill onto faces and surfaces.
Look: Photorealistic live-action, with natural skin texture and real fabric and metal. No CGI look, no plastic skin, no glossy game-engine light.
Contrast: Low-key chiaroscuro throughout the night interiors. Highlights stay on faces and hands in the centre third.
⑤ Sound Direction

Concrete Environmental & Foley SFX:

Scene 1: A deep, low time-lapse rumble; day ambience dissolving into crickets and night wind; nocturnal birds over the stone battlements.
Scene 2:
Gentle hum of the hologram; dry rustle of parchment; compass gears clicking.
A violent wooden bang as the double doors crash open; torches flaring in the draught.
Metallic slap of scabbards against brocade sashes; boot heels pacing the stone.
Two blades ringing out as the guards draw.
Scene 3:
A relentless, abrasive screech as the single scabbard tip of the sheathed Ancestral Sword gouges the flagstones.
The rhythmic cadence of the guards' steps; the soft hiss of burning torches.
Scene 4:
Grinding of the relic's turning rings.
A crystalline rush of hologram ocean, then a sharp crack as the northern gate fractures.
Steel scraping as it clears the scabbard; a quiet slice as the skin parts at the throat.
A deep resonant chime from the sunstone as it answers the mark.
A single whoosh as every torch gutters at once, then the violet pulse throbbing in dead silence before the hard cut.

Silence Strategy: Total silence the instant Agnivesh's finger touches the vibrating blade. All room reverb cuts out, leaving only Ranvijay's sharp, panicked intake of breath. A second silence sits under the final violet pulse, ending on the hard cut.

⑥ Transitions & Visual Continuity

Inter-Scene Transitions:

Ep 1 to Scene 1: Ep 1 ends on the hard cut on the glowing wrist mark. Ep 2 opens directly on the daylight palace time-lapse.
Scene 1 to Scene 2: Match dissolve from the palace's central dome under the full moon into the archive's vaulted ceiling, where the crane down in shot 2 begins.
Scene 2 to Scene 3: Straight cut, following Devika's stride as she walks out through the stone archway at the back of the archive.
Scene 3 to Scene 4: A continuous flow cut as the procession steps through the chamber doorway.
Scene 4 Climax: A crash zoom onto the violet symbol pulsing in the dark, then HARD CUT to black. No freeze-frame, no fade.

Visual Continuity Anchors:

Agnivesh's Attire:
His exact Ep 1 outfit throughout: fitted deep royal-blue silk angrakha with full-length sleeves and gold zari cuffs, sleek polished silver-and-gold breastplate with engraved lotus-vine patterns and the sun-mandala boss, layered silver shoulder guards, engraved silver-and-gold waist guard, ivory silk dhoti with a gold border, maroon silk angavastram draped from one shoulder, single pearl mala, tall leather boots with silver shin guards, and the scorched right cuff. No scabbard, no weapon.
No scabbard and no weapon in any shot.
The Ancient Book does not appear in Ep 2; his hands stay free throughout.
Devika's Attire: Turquoise-and-gold warrior attire with only Devika's Dagger at her belt. The Dual Short-Swords do not appear in Ep 2.
The Ancestral Sword:
Sc 2: thrust through Ranvijay's sash, hilt at his right hand.
Sc 3: sheathed in his right hand, scabbard tip dragging.
Sc 4: slid back into the sash on entering, then drawn right-handed to Agnivesh's throat, swung down, and raised for the charge.
Ranvijay's own talwar stays in its dark-red scabbard at his left hip and is never drawn.
Devika's Tools:
Sc 2: compass in hand. She sets it on the table before parting the brothers, then picks it up again.
Sc 3: the folded map and the compass in her hands.
Sc 4: the map unrolled over the relic, the compass open on the floor by her right knee, picked up in her left hand when she rises.
The Mark:
From the first archive shot: the scorched right cuff is already pulled down over the hidden mark (time has passed since Ep 1, bridged by the time-lapse).
Sc 2: a faint glow pulsing through the silk only (7); the cuff stays down.
Sc 4: the sleeve slides back and the mark glows gold as the sunstone answers (42).
The Wound: A thin line of blood at the front-left of Agnivesh's throat, below the jaw, from the moment he steps into the blade (40) until the end.
Light:
Sc 1: day turning to moonlit night.
Sc 2 to Sc 4: night lamp and torchlight plus the hologram glow.
After the gutter, the violet glow is the only light.
⑦ Derivative Assets Pre-Planning List
Asset Name	Derivative State	Reason / Narrative Appearance
Agnivesh	Scorched Cuff (Mark Hidden)	Scorched right cuff pulled down over the mark. His default state from the first archive shot (2) until he steps into the blade (40).
Agnivesh	Scorched Cuff + Throat Nick	Same outfit, with a thin line of blood at the front-left of the throat below the jaw. Sc 4, from shot 40 to the end.
Rajmahal Exterior	Moonlit Night	Identical framing at night, with the full moon over the central domes. Last frame of the Sc 1 time-lapse; the base is the first frame.
Royal Archives	Reverse View From the Doors	From the double doors looking down the table to the far end, the shelves and the stone archway. Master angle for Sc 2 (the base plate looks toward the doors).
Archive Ward Chamber	Reverse View Toward the Door	From beyond the relic looking at the chamber door. Used for the entry and Ranvijay's position by the door (Sc 4).
Swarnadweep Hologram	Northern Gate Breach	The northern gate split by a violet crack and jammed, its seawater turned black, dark mist curling in, and its part of the dome dark. End frame of the breach (Sc 4).

Reused existing (no new card):

Agnivesh / Scorched Cuff Glowing Mark (shot 42).
Swarnadweep Hologram, also used for the seven-gate projection over the archive table (Sc 2).

Handled in video, no card:

The relic's rings turning.
The compass needle spinning.
The drawn blade and the sunstone flicker (from the Ancestral Sword base).
The torch gutter and darkness (from the Archive Ward Chamber base)
